transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-08-30 15:00 UTC
Duration: 58 mins
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Rajiv (Redwood SE), Lina (Redwood DevAdv), Alex (Sparrow Head of Search), Dana (Sparrow ML), Tom (Sparrow Infra), Priya (PM)

Summary (auto): quick hosted API demo of embeddings + rerank flow; discuss integration steps, perf tradeoffs, security questions, pilot scope and next steps.

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, we'll run a short walkthrough of hosted embeddings + the rerank endpoint and show how you'd wire it into Sparrow's search layer.
[00:18] Alex: thanks, yeah we wanna see the end-to-end path — embed, index, retrieve, then rerank. we care a lot about tail latency and cost.
[00:28] Rajiv: great, we'll start with the API sequence: embeddings call, then a similarity index (we'll demo faiss-like semantics but note Redwood returns vectors you can plug into your index), then a /rerank endpoint that takes top-k candidates and scores them with a small cross-encoder on the server side.
[00:46] Dana: quick Q, is the rerank done on the same hosted instance as embeddings or a separate service?
[00:55] Rajiv: good question — on hosted mode the rerank model runs in the same multi-tenant service but we pin model variants for consistency; there is also a dedicated option if you want deterministic capacity. for pilot hosted is fine.
[01:15] Tom: any single-tenant requirement for us? we have strict data residency needs for user PII.
[01:24] Maya: we heard that — there's an option for Redwood Private (VPC) but for most customers we do encryption at-rest and optional customer-managed KMS; we'll share the SOC2 + KMS docs after call.
[01:38] Priya: timeline question — if pilot goes well, how quickly can we get Dedicated?
[01:43] Maya: typically a 4–6 week timeline for Dedicated onboarding, faster if infra changes are small.
[01:49]
--- Demo walk-through ---

[02:05] Rajiv: okay switching to the console, you can see a route for embeddings.create and a separate route for rerank.score. I'll paste sample curl calls in chat.
[02:22] Rajiv: (shares link) https://console.redwood.ai/examples/sparrow-embed-rerank — this is a playbook not a live copy.
[02:33] Lina: note we have a couple of templates for small cross-encoders vs late-fusion scoring; we'll recommend cross-encoder for high precision on the top 10 results.
[02:50] Alex: cross-encoder adds latency, right? how bad?
[02:55] Rajiv: depends on model size. our hosted small cross-encoder gives ~120–180ms p50 on 1x gpu profile for rerank of top10. you'll see p95 stretch — we usually recommend batching and async fallbacks.
[03:16] Dana: are the p95 numbers influenced more by queueing or model compute?
[03:21] Rajiv: both; queueing is the big variable. Redwood Optimize suggests batching windows by analyzing your query distribution — you can trade off a few ms for big cost wins.
[03:36]
[04:00] Alex: for Sparrow we have an e-commerce use case with many bursty queries during drops. burst handling is my main worry.
[04:08] Maya: we can set up autoscaling and burst capacity, you can also route critical traffic to a hotter dedicated pool while lower-tier traffic uses hosted.
[04:20] Tom: how does KV cache interact with rerank? like, can we cache embedding results?
[04:28] Rajiv: yes we have prefix and KV caching. typical pattern: cache embeddings for static docs and cache rerank scores for very frequent queries. but watch staleness — we expose TTL controls.
[04:39]
[05:05] (Lina shares a quick notebook example)
[05:12] Lina: here's a python snippet — call /v1/embeddings, then upsert to your vector DB; when a user query arrives, run search, then call /v1/rerank with top_k ids + context.
[05:28] Alex: what about using Redwood vector store vs us using Pinecone / Milvus?
[05:34] Rajiv: you can use whichever. many customers use Redwood embeddings + external vector DBs. we also partner with hosted vector indexes like Pinecone; if you choose to offload, we pass vectors and metadata and you keep the index.
[05:50] Alex: ok, so architecture-wise we could keep our current Faiss cluster and just swap in Redwood embeddings.
[05:54] Dana: does Redwood do on-the-fly dimension reduction or PCA? we have 1536 dim dense vectors and storage is a concern.
[06:05] Rajiv: we do quantization recommendations — Optimize will suggest 8-bit or 4-bit quantized embeddings for storage- and retrieval-cost tradeoffs. we don't silently transform vectors without telling you.
[06:18]
[06:45] Tom: network-level question: outbound traffic from Redwood hosted to our index — is that allowed?
[06:52] Maya: hosted mode expects you to host the index; Redwood returns vectors and the rerank endpoint can do scoring on our side — if you want zero egress we can do Private (VPC) or run an on-prem agent.
[07:05] Priya: can you show the rerank API payload?
[07:10] Rajiv: sure, sample: POST /v1/rerank {"query": "...", "candidates": [{"id": "123", "content":"...","embedding": [...]}, ...], "policy": "cross-encoder-small"} — we'll paste exact in chat.
[07:32] (background overlap)
[07:40] Alex: hmm in our infra it's nicer to pass candidate ids vs full embeddings to avoid payload size. is there a pull mode?
[07:47] Rajiv: yes, rerank can accept ids and Redwood will fetch the vectors if you store them in a Redwood-managed index; if you use external index, you pass vectors or content.
[08:02]
[08:30] Dana: about accuracy — any recommended prompt patterns or features to include in the reranker payload?
[08:38] Lina: include user signals and metadata fields; structured context with product attributes improves rerank. also consider synthetic negative mining in your fine-tuning loop.
[08:50] Alex: what's the feedback loop look like if we want continuous improvement?
[08:55] Rajiv: Redwood has evals integration — you can push labeled judgment sets, run A/Bs, and Optimize will suggest model and quantization changes if quality drops.
[09:10]
[09:40] Priya: security quickfire — SSO? RBAC? audit logs?
[09:47] Maya: yes SAML SSO supported, RBAC with role tiers, audit logs retained per plan; for enterprise we support HSM-backed KMS. I'll attach the compliance packet.
[09:58] Tom: we need log retention for 12 months and immutable audit trails. possible?
[10:04] Maya: offered on enterprise packages.
[10:07]
--- Performance run-through / mini benchmark ---

[10:30] Rajiv: let's run a small live sample. we'll send 10 queries through the hosted route with top-20 retrieval then rerank top-10.
[10:45] (we run test; occasional speech)
[11:05] Rajiv: results — median end-to-end 210ms, p95 ~540ms, cost per query estimate ~ $0.004 depending on model and batch.
[11:20] Alex: p95 is high for us, that's potentially too slow for search UX.
[11:25] Rajiv: understood. you can reduce p95 with a smaller cross-encoder, shard rerank across replicas, or pre-filter candidates more aggressively. Also try async rerank where we show an initial result and update after rerank.
[11:42] Dana: can you show batching knobs in the console?
[11:47] Rajiv: under Optimize -> Batching you'll see suggested windows based on your distribution. it suggests a 30ms micro-batch for your spike profile which should reduce token cost.
[12:02]
[12:35] Priya: cost modeling — how should we budget for a 10M queries/month workload?
[12:44] Maya: rough back-of-envelope: embeddings + storage + rerank. we'll send a detailed spreadsheet but ballpark hosted embeds 10M @ $X per 1k (example) plus rerank compute — total depends on top-k and model size. we'll share modeled scenarios.
[13:02] Alex: please include a dedicated vs hosted TCO comparison.
[13:06] Maya: yes will do.
[13:10]
--- Integration details / pitfalls ---

[13:35] Dana: we have multi-language queries + code snippets in content — any caveats?
[13:42] Rajiv: embeddings handle unicode; for code blocks we recommend a tokenization pre-process to keep semantics. Also be careful with stop-words removal prior to embedding.
[13:58] Tom: our infra uses strict egress rules — if we use hosted we'll need an allowlist for Redwood IPs. how quick is that setup?
[14:08] Maya: a few business days once frozen IPs are provided. Private is easier if you can't open outbound.
[14:18]
[14:50] (Priya notes a slide link in chat)
[15:00] Priya: ok on the security doc link, looks good.
[15:05]
--- Questions from Sparrow ---

[15:30] Alex: 1) How do you handle duplicates in the index? 2) Cold-start for new docs, and 3) A/B testing for rerank models.
[15:42] Rajiv: 1) we recommend dedup pipeline during ingestion with fingerprinting, 2) cold-start — run a mini-embed batch and use caching; Optimize suggests warmup profiles, 3) we support canary A/B via routing policies in Console.
[16:05]
[16:40] Dana: curious about latency consistency if we move to Dedicated.
[16:45] Maya: Dedicated gives predictable p50/p95 with SLA; you still need good batching and sizing but variability is much lower.
[16:54]
[17:20] Alex: any red flags we should watch for during the pilot?
[17:25] Rajiv: watch tail queueing during bursts, mis-sized batch windows, and forgetting to TTL cache stale rerank scores. we'll help instrument those via traces.
[17:40]
[18:05] (Lina shares notebook link)
[18:12] Lina: here's a simple test harness: https://gitlab.com/redwood/examples/sparrow-emb-rerank-harness (private link) — it includes a runner for batch embedding and rerank scoring.
[18:30] Alex: perfect we'll try.
[18:35]
--- Wrap-up / Recap ---

[18:50] Maya: quick recap: Redwood will send security packet + pricing + sample benchmark spreadsheet; Rajiv to produce runbook for batching and rerank tips; Sparrow will provide sample corpus and queries. target pilot start ~ 2026-09-07.
[19:10] Priya: timeline works for us as long as we get the sample spreadsheet and docs this week.
[19:18] Maya: I'll send the docs today.
[19:22] Alex: thanks everyone, that was helpful.
[19:27] (meeting ends)
